purpose: Historical benchmark and prototype measurements that motivated Crosscurrent. Do not treat bot-specific measurements as exact game-theoretic results.

caveats: Existing completed games were re-scored; bots were not retrained to adapt.
The game was not re-solved under the adjusted payoff.
Balancing mean score and balancing win probability are different objectives.
The normal six-deal alternating partie was already near 50/50.

mirror_policy_failure.exploit_description: Bid one above the prize value when possible, with the tested special handling around prize 13 / bid 1.
mirror_policy_failure.lesson: Perfect self-play balance can coexist with trivial exploitability.

tactical_vs_builder.builder_description: Evaluated deployments but did not use Shift or Recall.

tiny_exact_variant.caveat: Warning about mirror-draw equilibria; does not establish the full game's equilibrium draw rate.

tactical_position.tested_best_action: Shift 9 from B to C, paying 7
tactical_position.contrast: Shifting Q from A to B lost against every legal opponent reply in the tested position.

reduced_exact_variants.three_front: all-draw optimal equilibrium observed in solved reduced game
reduced_exact_variants.two_front: all-draw optimal equilibrium observed in solved reduced game
reduced_exact_variants.caveat: Reduced-game equilibrium behavior does not establish the full thirteen-rank game's optimal draw rate.

interpretation_rules: Structural symmetry is proved by rules, not by self-play statistics.
Full-size bot results are not proofs of optimal play.
Reduced variants explicitly labeled exact may support exact claims only for those reduced games.
A 50/50 expected result does not imply a short series will finish near 50/50.
Draw rate is policy-dependent unless established under solved optimal play.
research_integrity_notes: An earlier qualitative claim that Piquet was roughly 80–90% skill/variance was later found unsupported and must not be cited as evidence.
Piquet agency was qualitatively located in exchange decisions, declaration information, trick timing/suit forcing, and scoring-risk management.

crosscurrent_2026_audit_of_v02.evidence: Simulation with particular bots unless marked exact. Final-turn figures are exact solutions of positions sampled from bot play.
crosscurrent_2026_audit_of_v02.harness: research/sim (Rust); seats alternate; draws count one half; 95% intervals

bot.name: mctsx:N
bot.description: Simultaneous-move MCTS with regret matching (outcome sampling), N iterations per decision, final turn solved exactly by linear programming

expert_deep_vs_tactical.finding: Deep was not stronger than Tactical

scripted_probes_vs_mctsx4000_with_final_.note: Values are mctsx:4000's result. lowfirst also lost 97% to mctsx:16000, beat Casual 78.5% and lost to Tactical 84.8%.

crosscurrent_2026_rule_variant_study.evidence: Simulation with particular bots unless marked exact. Final-turn figures are exact solutions of positions sampled from bot self-play. Exact reduced-game values are exact for those reduced games only.
crosscurrent_2026_rule_variant_study.harness: research/sim (Rust); seats alternate; draws count one half; 95% intervals; logs and scripts in research/results
crosscurrent_2026_rule_variant_study.metric_note: stronger_expected_result_pct is the stronger bot's result with a draw counted one half: the chance that one game names the stronger bot if a draw were settled by a coin. Outright wins alone can rise without it when a tiebreak splits former draws evenly.

pairings.plain 4k vs 1k: mcts:4000 vs mcts:1000 (no exact final turn)

crosscurrent_2026_rule_variant_study.screening_protocol: mctsx:4000 vs mctsx:1000 (400 or 600 games), mctsx:4000 self-play (400), exact final-turn analysis of 400 self-play positions; sweep 1 also mctsx:16000 vs mctsx:4000 (400) and mctsx:4000 vs random (200)
crosscurrent_2026_rule_variant_study.finalist_protocol: fresh seeds: 4k vs 1k (1,200), 16k vs 4k (600), plain 4k vs 1k (600), self-play (600), final-turn analysis (600); sweep 6 adds controls and a second batch (4k vs 1k 2,400, 16k vs 4k 600, plain 1,200) for the tiebreak candidates

adopted.name: v0.3
adopted.tiebreak: total strength on all fronts summed over the three scorings, then draw
adopted.status: Adopted on simulation evidence; not yet tested with human players.

crosscurrent_vs_gops_2026.evidence: Simulation with one search bot for both games unless marked exact. Exact rows solve small decks completely (one equilibrium; others may exist). Last-decision rows solve exactly the last real decision of positions sampled from bot self-play.
crosscurrent_vs_gops_2026.harness: research/sim (Rust); one SM-MCTS implementation (src/search.rs) searches both games; seats alternate; draws count one half; 95% intervals; logs and scripts in research/results

bot_settings.crosscurrent: mctsx defaults: rollouts deploy 90% of the time, exploration 0.2, purification 0.1 (rechecked on v0.3 in gops-tuning.log)
bot_settings.gops: rollouts bid the card nearest the prize 80% of the time, exploration 0.2, purification 0.2 (chosen by head-to-head duels in gops-tuning.log)

crosscurrent_vs_gops_2026.gops_rules: 13 cards each, prizes 1-13 shuffled and revealed one at a time, higher bid scores the prize, ties score for nobody, no tiebreak; gops+asc reveals the prizes in ascending order
crosscurrent_vs_gops_2026.protocol: fresh seeds per game: 4k vs 1k (2,400 games), 16k vs 4k (1,200), plain 4k vs 1k (1,200), 64k vs 16k (400), 4k self-play (1,200), exact last decision of 1,200 self-play positions; the ladder pools the first three pairings. Robustness: 4k vs 1k (1,200 games) under other bot settings (run-gops-robustness.sh)
crosscurrent_vs_gops_2026.caveat: Bot-specific. Below 64,000 iterations the GOPS bot loses to the fixed rule 'bid one above the prize', so the GOPS figures describe this search family more than strong GOPS play. Iteration counts are not equal reasoning across games. No human games.
